metadata.description: Experimental gas-phase vibrational frequency and thermochemistry reference dataset for validating a MACE web app's vibrational-frequency/thermochemistry feature.
metadata.primary_source: NIST CCCBDB (https://cccbdb.nist.gov), 'Experimental Data' page per species (exp2x.asp?casno=<CAS number, no dashes>)
metadata.element_coverage_check: All molecules use only H, C, N, O -- a strict subset of MACE-OFF23's supported elements (H,C,N,O,F,P,S,Cl,Br,I).

units.zero_point_energy: cm^-1 (as-reported by CCCBDB), converted here also to kJ/mol and kcal/mol using 1 cm^-1 = 0.0119627 kJ/mol = 0.00285911 kcal/mol
units.entropy: J mol^-1 K^-1 at 298.15 K, 1 bar

important_caveats: CCCBDB's per-species 'vibrational zero-point energy' is computed as half the sum of the EXPERIMENTAL FUNDAMENTALS shown on the same page, not half the sum of true harmonic frequencies. It is a useful, fully-experimental number, but it is not the same quantity a harmonic MACE Hessian calculation produces (which sums half the HARMONIC frequencies). See each molecule's zero_point_energy.methodNote.

Rotational symmetry numbers are not tabulated per-species by CCCBDB; they were derived by combining the point group CCCBDB reports for each species with CCCBDB's own general symmetry-number-by-point-group table (thermox.asp). This derivation step is marked sourceType='computed' even though the underlying point group is experimental.

Methanol and ethanol both have a low-frequency CH3 (and, for ethanol, OH) internal rotation that is only approximately described as a harmonic torsional mode; CCCBDB lists it that way (200 cm^-1 for methanol; 251 and 200 cm^-1 for ethanol) but a rigorous treatment would use a hindered-rotor partition function with its own internal symmetry number (3 for a methyl top), separate from the overall external rotational symmetry number recorded here.

All numeric molecule data below was retrieved via automated fetch of the cited CCCBDB URLs; every fetched value was cross-checked for internal consistency (mode-count sums against 3N-6/3N-5, sum-of-fundamentals against the reported ZPE) and against well-established textbook/NIST-JANAF values before being included. No value was invented; where a page could not be retrieved this is stated instead of a fabricated number.

CCCBDB was reachable directly via automated fetch for every one of the 10 target species (exp2x.asp?casno=...); the NIST Chemistry WebBook fallback described in the task instructions was not needed for the core vibrational/entropy/ZPE dataset.

scaling_factor_guidance.question: What frequency scaling factor is appropriate when comparing computed harmonic frequencies to experimental fundamentals?
scaling_factor_guidance.answer_summary: Computed harmonic frequencies are systematically higher than experimental fundamental frequencies for two independent reasons: (1) the real potential energy surface is anharmonic (better approximated by a Morse-like potential near a bond-stretch minimum), which by itself lowers the observed fundamental (v=0->1) transition below the harmonic value omega_e; and (2) the electronic structure method/reference itself carries some error relative to the true PES. Because both effects push in the same direction, a single empirical multiplicative scale factor (typically in the range 0.8-1.0) is conventionally applied to harmonic frequencies before comparison to experiment. CCCBDB's own compiled scale factors for well-behaved methods cluster around 0.95-0.99 (HF ~0.90 -- large correction because HF also has large systematic method error on top of anharmonicity; MP2 ~0.94-0.96; B3LYP ~0.96-0.97; PBE-type GGA functionals ~0.98-0.99; CCSD(T) with a large basis ~0.98-0.99, i.e. closest to a pure anharmonicity-only correction since method error is small at that level). CCCBDB explicitly notes that different scale factors are appropriate for low- and high-frequency vibrations, i.e. a single flat number is itself an approximation, and that scale factors carry their own reported uncertainty.
scaling_factor_guidance.why_anharmonicity_lowers_the_fundamental: For a Morse-like oscillator with the same curvature (second derivative) at the minimum as the harmonic approximation, the vibrational levels G(v) = omega_e(v+1/2) - omega_e*x_e(v+1/2)^2 + ... are more closely spaced than harmonic levels; the anharmonic constant term is subtracted, so the observed 0->1 fundamental transition frequency is always somewhat below the underlying harmonic frequency omega_e. This is a physical effect present even for an exact solution of a given PES, distinct from any error in the electronic structure method used to generate that PES.

sources.claim: General framework: scale factors in range 0.8-1.0 correct for both approximate electronic structure and PES anharmonicity; Morse-potential / G(v) anharmonic term explanation.
Different scale factors are appropriate for low- and high-frequency vibrations; scale factors are tabulated with associated uncertainties by method/basis set.
Representative literature scale factor value for a range-separated hybrid functional (wB97X-D/3-21G*) = 0.955, illustrating the ~0.95-0.98 band typical of high-quality DFT.

Widely-cited independent scale-factor compilation and recommended values/uncertainties for many electronic model chemistries (harmonic frequency, fundamental frequency, and ZPE scale factors treated as distinct quantities).
sources.citation: Alecu, I. M.; Zheng, J.; Zhao, Y.; Truhlar, D. G. Computational Thermochemistry: Scale Factor Databases and Scale Factors for Vibrational Frequencies Obtained from Electronic Model Chemistries. J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2010, 6, 2872-2887.

mace_off23_documented_accuracy.question: What accuracy is MACE-OFF23 actually documented to achieve on vibrational frequencies?
mace_off23_documented_accuracy.answer_summary: We could not find any published number for MACE-OFF23's frequency or ZPE error measured AGAINST EXPERIMENT. Every quantitative benchmark located compares MACE-OFF23 (or the wider MACE model family) against a DFT reference, not against experimental fundamentals. State plainly: no MACE-OFF23-vs-experiment frequency MAE currently exists in the literature that we could locate; any tolerance used to validate this feature is therefore necessarily informed by (a) MACE-vs-DFT benchmarks and (b) the independent, method-agnostic harmonic-vs-experimental-fundamental gap documented by CCCBDB/Truhlar-style scale-factor studies, not by a single MACE-specific ground-truth number.

findings.source: Kovacs, D. P. et al. MACE-OFF: Short-Range Transferable Machine Learning Force Fields for Organic Molecules. arXiv:2312.15211 (also published as J. Am. Chem. Soc. 2025, 147, 17598-17611).
findings.finding: The original MACE-OFF23 paper's abstract references 'accurate secondary structure and vibrational spectrum' qualitatively (in the context of a solvated protein MD run) but does not report a quantitative vibrational-frequency MAE/RMSE figure. No numeric frequency accuracy claim from this primary paper could be confirmed.

findings.source: Pracht, P.; Pillai, Y.; Kapil, V.; Csanyi, G.; Gonnheimer, N.; Vondrak, M.; Margraf, J. T.; Wales, D. J. Efficient Composite Infrared Spectroscopy: Combining the Double-Harmonic Approximation with Machine Learning Potentials. J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2024, 20 (24), 10986-11004.
findings.finding: On the IR7193 benchmark set (7193 gas-phase molecules, 3-77 atoms, elements H,C,N,O,F,Cl,Br,S,P), MACE-OFF23 zero-point vibrational energy (ZPVE) was reported with MAE = 0.22-0.23 kcal/mol and RMSE = 0.30-0.31 kcal/mol relative to a B3LYP-3c DFT reference (NOT experiment). Small/medium/large MACE-OFF23 sizes performed similarly. This is the most concrete numeric MACE-OFF23 vibrational accuracy figure we located, but it is a DFT-reference ZPVE error, not a per-mode frequency MAE and not an experimental comparison.

findings.source: Suarez-Dou, S.; Gallegos, M.; Han, K.; Brunig, F. N.; Berryman, J. T.; Tkatchenko, A. Quantum-Accurate Conformational Stabilities and Vibrational Dynamics in Molecules and Proteins with Machine-Learned Force Fields. arXiv:2601.09845 (2026).
findings.finding: Introduces the QVib benchmark (293 molecules, 1365 conformers) referenced against PBE0+MBD DFT (again NOT experiment). Reports qualitatively that 'the MACE family provides the best overall agreement with the reference across both frequency MAE and IR-spectrum similarity metrics' among tested MLFFs, but flags that roughly 257/293 (~90%) of the benchmark molecules have close chemical analogues in MACE-OFF23's training set, i.e. the reported strong performance is largely interpolative. No MACE-OFF23-specific aggregate cm^-1 MAE value could be extracted from the accessible text; a worked single-molecule example for a different model (SO3LR, aspartame) gives MAE = 8.2 cm^-1 vs PBE0+MBD, illustrating the achievable order of magnitude for a well-trained MLFF but not a MACE-OFF23 number itself.

mace_off23_documented_accuracy.conclusion: No experiment-referenced MACE-OFF23 frequency accuracy number exists in the literature we were able to retrieve. The only concrete MACE-OFF23 number found is a DFT-referenced ZPVE MAE of 0.22-0.23 kcal/mol (Pracht et al. 2024). Any pass/fail tolerance for this project's validator is therefore built from that DFT-reference figure plus the independent, well-established anharmonicity gap documented by CCCBDB (harmonic frequencies exceed experimental fundamentals by roughly 2-5%, larger in absolute cm^-1 for X-H stretches), not from a single MACE-OFF23-vs-experiment number, because that number does not appear to exist yet.

recommended_validation_tolerance.recommendation: Do not compare a raw MACE harmonic frequency directly to an experimental fundamental with a flat pass/fail cutoff. Instead: (1) apply a fixed scaling factor of 0.97 to every MACE harmonic frequency before comparison (mid-point of the 0.96-0.99 band CCCBDB reports for high-quality DFT/CCSD(T)-level methods, appropriate because MACE-OFF23 is trained on a high-quality DFT reference, wB97M-D3BJ, so method error should be small relative to the anharmonicity gap that scaling primarily corrects for); then (2) apply a pass/fail band on the SCALED frequency of +/-4% relative OR +/-50 cm^-1 absolute, whichever is larger, treating modes below ~1000 cm^-1 (bends, torsions, skeletal/ring modes) with the absolute 50 cm^-1 floor and modes above ~1000 cm^-1 (X-H stretches, C=O/C=C stretches) with the 4% relative band.
recommended_validation_tolerance.why_not_a_single_flat_cm-1_number: CCCBDB explicitly states that different scale factors are appropriate for low- and high-frequency vibrations, and the molecules in this dataset span torsions at ~200 cm^-1 (methanol, ethanol) to O-H/C-H stretches above 3600 cm^-1 (water, methanol, ethanol, benzene). A single absolute cm^-1 tolerance would be far too loose for a 200 cm^-1 torsion and far too tight for a 3800 cm^-1 stretch; a relative-percentage tolerance solves this but becomes unreasonably tight (a few cm^-1) for the lowest-frequency modes, hence the combined relative-OR-absolute floor.
quantitative_basis: CCCBDB-reported literature scale factors for high-quality methods: B3LYP ~0.96-0.97, PBE-type GGA ~0.98-0.99, CCSD(T)/large basis ~0.98-0.99, wB97X-D/3-21G* = 0.955 (https://cccbdb.nist.gov/vibscalejustx.asp, https://cccbdb.nist.gov/vibscale2x.asp?method=60&basis=8).

Pracht et al. 2024 (10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01157) report MACE-OFF23 ZPVE MAE 0.22-0.23 kcal/mol and RMSE 0.30-0.31 kcal/mol vs a B3LYP-3c DFT reference on the 7193-molecule IR7193 set; expressed per-mode, a 0.22 kcal/mol ZPVE MAE corresponds to a total half-sum-of-frequency error of about 77 cm^-1 across all modes of a molecule, i.e. a handful of cm^-1 per mode when spread over a typical small-molecule mode count -- this bounds MACE's OWN error relative to its DFT reference, separate from the DFT-vs-experiment anharmonicity gap the 0.97 scale factor is meant to absorb.

Water worked example from this dataset: experimental fundamental vs CCCBDB-tabulated spectroscopic harmonic frequency differs by -175 cm^-1 (4.8%) for the symmetric stretch (3657 vs 3832 cm^-1) and -187 cm^-1 (4.9%) for the asymmetric stretch (3756 vs 3943 cm^-1), and by -54 cm^-1 (3.4%) for the bend (1595 vs 1649 cm^-1) -- directly demonstrating the 3-5% anharmonicity gap the 0.97 scale factor targets, using this project's own cited CCCBDB numbers rather than an external assumption.
recommended_validation_tolerance.caveat: This tolerance is a considered engineering choice, not a validated MACE-OFF23-specific number, because (as documented above) no MACE-OFF23-vs-experiment frequency benchmark exists in the literature we could find. It should be revisited if such a benchmark is published, and it will likely need to be widened further for hindered-rotor modes (methanol/ethanol torsions below ~300 cm^-1), which a harmonic treatment handles poorly regardless of the underlying PES quality.
